_help.about: What the player can carry and wear (Inventory; the inventory screen on I). Restart the game after editing. Spec Appendix R4: a handful of items, weight felt in movement (movement table 'burden'), never read in a menu.
_help.sample_reach_m: How near a plant must be (from your hands) for E to take a sample of it.
_help.carry_slots: How many things you can carry. Each slot holds one thing: a bundle of herbs, a plant sample, a cut cactus column, a fish, a mushroom.
_help.starting_kit: What a NEW game puts in your hands at the opening fire (design §M, §T): the three tools of the whole game, worn in their slots, plus a quiver of arrows (data/combat.json quiver.start). There are no other tools, ever: no axes, picks, shovels, knives or stone tools, and no tool crafting. After a death you wake with nothing; the kit is on your corpse with the rest.
_help.equipment.pole: The fishing pole's slot: one worn, no spares (it is one of the three tools, not gear to collect).
_help.equipment: The slots you wear things in: how many are worn and how many spares each keeps (R4: one worn and two spares; rings two worn and two spares). Spares don't count as carried.
_help.kinds: Every kind of item: its name on the screen, the little picture drawn for it (icon), and which equipment slot it's worn in (slot; none = it's carried). color is the picture's main color where the item doesn't bring its own (a plant sample takes its species' colors).
_help.sample_part: What E on a plant takes, by the plant's shape: a cutting, a seed head, a leaf, or a cut column (a cactus: its own kind of item). Shapes not listed give a cutting.
_help.bundle_genera: Plants of these genera give a bundle of herbs (cut stems, tied) instead of a sample. It still carries the species.
